report.title: Kesko interim report 1.1.-30.9.2026: Kesko's profit improved significantly - technical trade continues as the driver

results.text: Our net sales totalled €3,394 million, representing an increase of 4.7% in comparable terms.
In the grocery trade division, net sales increased by 2.7% and totalled €1,690 million.
K Group’s grocery sales grew by 1.8%, while the total grocery market in Finland grew by approximately 0.6%.
Kespro’s net sales decreased by 1.0% as the foodservice market remained challenging, but Kespro managed to gain market share.
In the building and technical trade division, net sales grew in all operating countries, totalling €1,328 million.
The marked improvement in profit was attributable in particular to technical trade, where net sales grew by 11.3%, with sales growth being the strongest in Finland, Norway and Poland.

outlook.text: Kesko estimates that its 2026 comparable operating profit will amount to €690–‍730 million.
Our order book for new cars was up by nearly 70% year-on-year and by some 65% since the start of the year.
We are updating our profit guidance, and now estimate that Kesko’s comparable operating profit for 2026 will amount to €690–730 million, while our previous estimate was €670–730 million.

highlights: Group net sales in July–September totalled €3,394.5 million (€3,227.3 million); reported net sales grew by 5.2% while in comparable terms, net sales grew by 4.7%
Comparable operating profit totalled €231.4 million (€208.1 million), representing an increase of €23.3 million
Operating profit totalled €235.7 million (€204.0 million)
sections.outlook: Kesko Group’s profit guidance is given for the year 2026, in comparison with the year 2025. Kesko’s operating environment is estimated to improve in 2026, but to still remain somewhat challenging. Kesko’s comparable operating profit is estimated to improve in 2026. Kesko estimates that its 2026 comparable operating profit will amount to €690–‍730 million.

results.text: Matas Group delivered currency neutral revenue growth of 1.5% in Q2 2026/27, corresponding to reported growth of 2.4%.

sections.outlook: In Q2, we took important steps in the long-term business transformation of Matas Group, advancing the integration of KICKS and preparing for the launch of our new Nordic operating model on 1 October. results.text: The third quarter in brief Marimekko’s net sales in the third quarter increased by 3 percent and amounted to EUR 52.1 million (50.8).

Net sales in Finland decreased by 6 percent as the continued challenging market situation impacted negatively particularly domestic retail sales.
Comparable operating profit totaled EUR 23.4 million (23.5) equaling to 17.0 percent of net sales (17.5).

outlook.text: Financial guidance for 2026 (unchanged) The Marimekko Group’s net sales for 2026 are expected to grow from the previous year (2025: EUR 189.6 million).

Our financial guidance for 2026 remains unchanged: the Marimekko Group’s net sales for 2026 are expected to grow from the previous year, and the comparable operating profit margin is estimated to be approximately some 16–19 percent.

highlights: Marimekko’s net sales in the third quarter increased by 3 percent and amounted to EUR 52.1 million (50.8). Net sales were boosted especially by the excellent development of wholesale and retail sales in all international market areas.

Net sales in Finland decreased by 9 percent as especially wholesale sales declined in the continued challenging operating environment. In a price-sensitive market situation, retail sales in Finland also decreased.
International sales increased by 16 percent following the excellent development of net sales in all market areas.
sections.outlook: There are significant uncertainties related to the development of the global economy, such as tensions related to geopolitics and trade relations. results.text: Despite higher fixed costs, EBIT for the first nine months of the year amounted to DKK 977m, compared with DKK 785m in the corresponding period last year.
Profit & loss Revenue increased by 19% to DKK 5,807m in Q3 2026 from DKK 4,898m in Q3 2025, driven by higher volumes and increasing raw material prices, particularly marine fish oil and fish meal.

Revenue for the first nine months of 2026 increased by 7% to DKK 13,172m from DKK 12,270m year to date in Q3 2025, primarily reflecting higher volumes, raw material prices and product and customer mix.
Other costs and other operating income and expenses increased year on year in Q3 2026 from DKK 352m to DKK 432m.
For the first nine months of 2026, other costs and other operating income and expenses increased year on year from DKK 929m to DKK 1,121m, reflecting the same matters as above.
EBIT for Q3 2026 amounted to DKK 618m, compared with DKK 411m in Q3 2025, supported by higher feed volumes and significantly improved earnings in the Salmon segment especially.

outlook.text: Supported by the volume outlook, higher raw material prices and current exchange rates, BioMar raises its 2026 revenue guidance to DKK 17.8-18.6 billion range from previously DKK 17.0-18.0 billion.

Based on strong earnings momentum in the first nine months of 2026, but a lower volume guidance for 2026, increasing prices on ingredients, and uncertainties particularly related to Ecuador, BioMar is upgrading its EBIT guidance to DKK 1,290-1,360 million range from previously DKK 1,200-1,300 million.

highlights: Revenue rose 19% year on year to DKK 5,807 million, reflecting mainly higher volumes, higher raw material prices and a positive currency impact of DKK 228 million.

ROIC including goodwill increased to 27.1% (21.9%). NIBD/EBITDA was 1.37x (1.45x).

report.title: Valmet's Interim Review January 1 - September 30, 2026: Strong orders received and increased comparable EBITA

results.text: Earnings per share (EPS) decreased to EUR 0.38 (EUR 0.46) and adjusted EPS decreased to EUR 0.48 (EUR 0.54).
Comparable EBITA remained at the previous year’s level and was EUR 434 million (EUR 423 million).

In the third quarter, the trust they place in Valmet translated into strong demand: orders received increased 25 percent organically, while comparable EBITA reached a record level for a third quarter.
Comparable EBITA increased by EUR 10 million to EUR 169 million, supported by the Severn acquisition and the efficiency and cost reduction actions we are taking under our Lead the Way strategy.

outlook.text: By 2030, our target is to grow 5 percent organically and reach a 15 percent comparable EBITA margin.

highlights: • Orders received increased 30 percent to EUR 1,408 million (EUR 1,083 million). Organically orders received increased 25 percent.
• Net sales increased 5 percent to EUR 1,360 million (EUR 1,295 million).

• Comparable EBITA increased 6 percent to EUR 169 million (EUR 159 million). The increase was due to consolidation of Severn Group (now Engineered Severe Service) into Valmet as of July 1, 2026 and the positive impact of efficiency and cost reduction actions as part of the Lead the Way strategy.
sections.outlook: Valmet reiterates its guidance issued on February 6, 2026, in which Valmet estimates that net sales in 2026 will remain at the previous year's level in comparison with 2025 (EUR 5,197 million) and Comparable EBITA in 2026 will remain at the previous year's level or increase in comparison with 2025 (EUR 620 million).

outlook.text: Outlook for 2026 (last updated on June 10, 2026) REVENUE Kemira's revenue is expected to be between EUR 2,600 and EUR 3,000 million in 2026 (2025 revenue: EUR 2,753.5 million).
OPERATIVE EBITDA Kemira's operative EBITDA is expected to be between EUR 400 and EUR 500 million in 2026 (2025 operative EBITDA: EUR 524.6 million).

We reiterate our financial outlook for the year and expect our 2026 revenue to be between EUR 2,600 million and EUR 3,000 million and our 2026 operative EBITDA to be between EUR 400 million and EUR 500 million.

Financial targets Kemira has the following long-term financial targets to support its growth strategy; Kemira’s target is to achieve an annual organic growth rate of over 4%, to maintain an operative EBITDA margin within the range of 18–21% and to maintain operative ROCE above 16%.

highlights: • Revenue increased by 3%, amounting to EUR 708.9 million (687.7), mainly driven by acquisitions. Revenue in local currencies, excluding acquisitions and divestmen ts, was stable.

• Operative EBITDA decreased by 18%, to EUR 112.8 million (137.3). Operative EBITDA margin was 15.9% (20.0%). The decrease resulted mainly from cost inflation following the conflict in the Middle East.
• Operative EBITDA margin declined to 19.7% in Water Solutions (23.1%), to 9.3% in Packaging & Hygiene Solutions (13.6%) and to 19.3% in Fiber Essentials (24.1%).
sections.outlook: The demand in Kemira's end-markets remains weak due to continued global economic uncertainty and geopolitical tensions and the raw material and logistics cost environment continues to be volatile. The outlook assumes that the negative impact of raw material and logistics cost inflation on Kemira's full-year 2026 cost base is around EUR 100 million, of which roughly 50% will be covered by price increases.

results.text: The insurance service result was supported by reported revenue growth of 4.1% with the highest growth recorded in the Private segment.
Insurance revenue Insurance revenue amounted to DKK 10,591m (DKK 10,175m), corresponding to a growth of 2.3% (3.4%) in local currencies.
This was driven by the Private segment growing 3.7% (3.8%) measured in local currencies with organic growth in selected segments, for instance in Private Norway.
Revenue growth was 4.1% measured in DKK, or 2.3% in local currencies, with the highest growth in Norway.

Q1-Q3 2026 results Insurance revenue growth of 3.0% (3.7%) measured in local currencies was mainly driven by portfolio growth in selected segments and profitability initiatives to mitigate inflation, particularly in Private Norway.

highlights: Insurance revenue growth of 5.0% in DKK, or 3.0% in local currencies (3.7% in local currencies)
Profit before tax of DKK 4,476m (DKK 5,505m), or DKK 5,676m adjusted for the one-off provision on Danish workers' compensation booked in Q2 2026

report.title: Q1 Trading Statement 2026/27:  Bang & Olufsen generated revenue growth of 2.2% in local currencies

results.text: EBITDA before special items was DKK 42m (DKK 34m), with an EBITDA margin before special items of 8.0% (6.5%).
EBIT before special items was DKK -23m (DKK -27m), with an EBIT margin before special items of -4.3% (-5.2%).
Revenue was DKK 226m compared to DKK 234m in Q1 last year, representing a decline of 3.4% or 3.6% in local currencies.
Revenue was DKK 62m, unchanged from Q1 last year, representing a decline of 0.4% or 1.4% in local currencies.
Revenue was DKK 177m compared to DKK 159m in Q1 last year, representing an increase of 11.7% or 11.5% in local currencies.
Revenue from China increased by 10.3% year-on-year, equivalent to growth of 2.9% in local currencies and accounting for approximately 50% of total revenue in APAC.

outlook.text: Page — 1 Trading statement Q1 2026/27 June 2026-August 2026 Page — 2 Management’s review Q1 2026/27 In Q1 2026/27, Bang & Olufsen generated revenue growth of 2.2% in local currencies, in line with expectations.

highlights: In Q1 2026/27, Bang & Olufsen generated revenue growth of 2.2% in local currencies, in line with expectations. The gross margin rose to a new peak of 59.4%, an increase of 0.7 percentage points from last year.
events: Opening of our largest store in Asia Pacific at Scotts Square in Singapore in June, the first location of our Culture Store concept in Southeast Asia.
Opening of our 260 m² store in Palo Alto, California, in August, completing the three planned California openings alongside our San Francisco and West Hollywood flagships.
